proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an admissible path \(P_t\) and write \(r_t=dP_t/dP\) and \(z_t=\sqrt{r_t}-1\).  By DQM, \(z_t=ts/2+o_{L^2(P)}(t)\), and hence \(\|z_t\|_2=O(|t|)\).  The likelihood-ratio ball in \(\mathrm{def:local-operator-chart}\), together with \(0<\varepsilon<1\), bounds \(r_t\) above and away from zero, so \(\sup_t\|z_t\|_\infty<\infty\) locally.  Therefore every fixed \(f\in L^2(P)\) satisfies
\[
 E_{P_t}f-E_Pf
 =E_P\{f(2z_t+z_t^2)\}
 =tE_P(fs)+o(t).
\]
Indeed, the linear term follows by Cauchy--Schwarz.  For the quadratic term, for every \(M>0\),
\[
 \frac{E_P(|f|z_t^2)}{|t|}
 \le M\frac{\|z_t\|_2^2}{|t|}
 +\|f\mathbf 1\{|f|>M\}\|_2
   \frac{\|z_t\|_\infty\|z_t\|_2}{|t|}.
\]
The first term tends to zero for fixed \(M\), the second has limsup bounded by a constant times \(\|f\mathbf 1\{|f|>M\}\|_2\), and this last norm tends to zero as \(M\to\infty\).  Thus the displayed expectation derivative is justified without assuming bounded bridges.

Put \(B_{h,q}=\sum_{a=0}^1t_aS_a(h_a,q_a)=\theta(P)+\phi_{h,q}\).  The base score is square-integrable by hypothesis, so the preceding calculation gives
\[
 E_{P_t}B_{h,q}-E_PB_{h,q}
 =tE_P(\phi_{h,q}s)+o(t),
\]
where \(E_Ps=0\) removes the centering constant.  It remains to compare \(E_{P_t}B_{h,q}\) with \(\theta(P_t)\).  First, the arm mean does not depend on the selected outcome bridge: if \(h_{a,t}'\) is another solution, then \(u=h_{a,t}'-h_{a,t}\in\ker T_{a,t}\), and any \(q_{a,t}\in\mathcal Q_a(P_t)\) gives
\[
 E_{P_t}u=E_{P_t}(I_aq_{a,t}u)
 =E_{P_t}\{I_aq_{a,t}T_{a,t}u\}=0.
\]
All products are integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz and the square-integrability of the two bridges under \(P_t\).  Thus \(\theta_a(P_t)=E_{P_t}h_{a,t}\) is well defined.  For one arm, outcome-bridge solvability under \(P_t\) gives
\[
 E_{P_t}\!\left[I_aq_a\{Y-h_{a,t}(W,X)\}\right]=0,
\]
because \(q_a\) is a function of \((Z,X)\) and \(E_{P_t}[Y-h_{a,t}(W,X)\mid A=a,Z,X]=0\).  Treatment-bridge solvability under \(P_t\) gives
\[
 E_{P_t}\!\left[(1-I_aq_{a,t})\{h_{a,t}(W,X)-h_a(W,X)\}\right]=0.
\]
Subtracting these two identities from the definition of \(S_a\) yields the exact mixed-bias identity
\[
 \theta_a(P_t)-E_{P_t}S_a(h_a,q_a)
 =E_{P_t}\!\left[I_a(q_{a,t}-q_a)(h_{a,t}-h_a)\right],
 \qquad \theta_a(P_t)=E_{P_t}h_{a,t}.
\]
Conditioning first on \((A,Z,X)\), or first on \((W,X)\), and applying Cauchy--Schwarz gives respectively
\[
 \left|\theta_a(P_t)-E_{P_t}S_a(h_a,q_a)\right|
 \le
 \|T_{a,t}(h_{a,t}-h_a)\|_{\mathcal G_a(P_t)}
 \|q_{a,t}-q_a\|_{\mathcal G_a(P_t)}
\]
and
\[
 \left|\theta_a(P_t)-E_{P_t}S_a(h_a,q_a)\right|
 \le
 \|h_{a,t}-h_a\|_{\mathcal H(P_t)}
 \|T_{a,t}^*(q_{a,t}-q_a)\|_{\mathcal H(P_t)}.
\]
The assumed minimum of these products is \(o(|t|)\) in each arm.  Taking the signed arm difference proves
\[
 \theta(P_t)-\theta(P)=tE_P(\phi_{h,q}s)+o(t).
\]
Thus \(\phi_{h,q}\) is a gradient on the actual score set, and continuity extends the representation to \(\mathcal T_P\).

By \(\mathrm{lem:normal-affine-identity}\), \(\mathcal A_P=\phi_0+\mathcal C_P\).  The point
\[
 \phi_* =\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0,
 \qquad \phi_*\perp\mathcal C_P.
\]
belongs to \(\phi_0+\mathcal C_P\).  For every \(c\in\mathcal C_P\), orthogonality gives
\[
 \|\phi_0+c\|_2^2
 =\|\phi_*\|_2^2+\|\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0+c\|_2^2,
\]
so \(\phi_*\) is the unique minimum-norm point.
The assumed tangent equality makes \(\phi_*\in\mathcal T_P\).  For \(v\in\mathcal T_P\),
\[
 E(\phi_*v)=E(\phi_0v)-E\{(\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0)v\}=\dot\theta_P(v),
\]
so \(\phi_*\) is the canonical gradient.  If \(g\in L_0^2(P)\) is any other gradient, then \(g-\phi_0\in\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal C_P\); conversely, every \(\phi_0+c\), \(c\in\mathcal C_P\), represents the same derivative.  Hence the gradient set is exactly \(\mathcal A_P\), and minimizing its squared norm proves both asserted formulas.  None of these steps proves that an arbitrary Riesz representer must be an individual bridge-pair score, which is why no converse is claimed.

For one learned cell write \(\Delta h=\widehat h-h^0\) and \(\Delta q=\widehat q-q^0\).  Direct expansion of the definition of \(S_a\) gives the exact equality
\[
 S_a(\widehat h,\widehat q)-S_a(h^0,q^0)
 =(1-I_aq^0)\Delta h+I_a(Y-h^0)\Delta q-I_a\Delta q\Delta h.
\]
Hölder's inequality, the construction-sample fourth-norm rates, and \(\mathrm{ass:moment-envelope-growth}\) therefore give
\[
 \|S_a(\widehat h,\widehat q)-S_a(h^0,q^0)\|_2
 \le M_{q,n}\|\Delta h\|_4+M_{y,n}\|\Delta q\|_4
 +\|\Delta h\|_4\|\Delta q\|_4
 =O_p(d^S_{a,j\ell,n}).
\]
Every dictionary coordinate is a signed sum of at most four cell signals.  The triangle inequality bounds its \(L^2(P)\) error by the corresponding \(d_{c,n}\).  Summing the squared coordinate bounds proves
\[
 \|\widehat D-D^0\|_{L^2(P;\ell^2)}^2
 =\sum_{c=1}^{J_n}\|\widehat D_c-D_c^0\|_2^2
 =O_p\!\left(\sum_{c=1}^{J_n}d_{c,n}^2\right),
\]
including the stated \(\sqrt{J_n}\) upper bound.  The same calculation for the two base cells gives \(\|\widehat B-B^0\|_2=O_p(d_{0,n})\), where \(B^0=\theta(P)+\phi_0\).

The calibration conclusions follow from \(\mathrm{lem:conditional-calibration-concentration}\), not from evaluation-fold independence.  Let \(G=E[D^0D^{0\top}]\), \(c=E[D^0B^0]\), and let \(\widetilde G=E[\widehat D\widehat D^\top\mid\mathcal D_{A,k}]\) and \(\widetilde c=E[\widehat D\widehat B\mid\mathcal D_{A,k}]\).  Cauchy--Schwarz for Hilbert-space-valued random variables gives
\[
 \|\widetilde G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le \|\widehat D-D^0\|_{L^2(\ell^2)}
 \{\|\widehat D\|_{L^2(\ell^2)}+\|D^0\|_{L^2(\ell^2)}\}
 \le 2\sqrt{J_n}B_{D,n}\delta_{D,n}+\delta_{D,n}^2
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde c-c\|_2
 \le B_{0,n}\delta_{D,n}+(\sqrt{J_n}B_{D,n}+\delta_{D,n})d_{0,n}.
\]
Combining these inequalities with calibration concentration yields
\[
 \|\widehat G_k^C-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(\zeta_{G,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat c_k^C-c\|_2=O_p(\zeta_{c,n}).
\]

All nonzero eigenvalues of \(G\) are at least \(\kappa_{J_n}\).  Since \(\zeta_{G,n}=o_p(\tau_n)\) and \(\tau_n<\kappa_{J_n}/2\), Weyl's variational inequality, obtained directly from \(|u^\top(\widehat G-G)u|\le\|\widehat G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), shows with probability tending to one that eigenvalues arising from \(\ker G\) lie below \(\tau_n\), whereas eigenvalues arising from its range exceed \(\kappa_{J_n}/2\).  Threshold \(\widehat G\) by replacing its eigenvalues at most \(\tau_n\) by zero.  The thresholded operator differs from \(G\) by \(O_p(\zeta_{G,n})\), and both reduced minimum moduli are at least \(\kappa_{J_n}/2\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:operator-kernel-perturbation}\) to these two finite-dimensional operators yields
\[
 \|\widehat\Pi_k^C-\Pi_{R,J_n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =O_p(\zeta_{G,n}/\kappa_{J_n})=O_p(\eta_{\Pi,n}).
\]

By definition, \(Gb_{J_n}=c\), \(b_{J_n}\in\operatorname{range}(G)\), and the cutoff equation is
\[
 (\widehat G_k^C+\rho_n I)\widehat b
 =\widehat\Pi_k^C\widehat c_k^C,
 \qquad \widehat b=\widehat\Pi_k^C\widehat b.
\]
Writing \(\Pi_R=\Pi_{R,J_n}\), using \(G(I-\Pi_R)=0\), and subtracting \(Gb_{J_n}=c\) gives the exact positive-eigenspace equation
\[
 G\Pi_R(\widehat b-b_{J_n})
 =\Pi_R\{(G-\widehat G_k^C)\widehat b
 +(\widehat c_k^C-c)-\rho_n\widehat b
 -(I-\widehat\Pi_k^C)\widehat c_k^C\}.
\]
Because \(c\in\operatorname{range}(G)\),
\[
 \|(I-\widehat\Pi_k^C)\widehat c_k^C\|_2
 \le \zeta_{c,n}+\eta_{\Pi,n}\|c\|_2,
 \qquad
 \|c\|_2\le\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}\,\|B^0\|_2
 \le\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}B_{0,n}.
\]
Inversion of \(G\) on its positive eigenspace and the coefficient envelope now give
\[
 \|\Pi_R(\widehat b-b_{J_n})\|_2
 \le \frac{C}{\kappa_{J_n}}
 \{\zeta_{c,n}+(\zeta_{G,n}+\rho_n)L_n
 +\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}B_{0,n}\eta_{\Pi,n}\}.
\]
Since \(\|v^\top D^0\|_2=\|G^{1/2}v\|_2\le\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}\|\Pi_Rv\|_2\), while \(\|\widehat b^\top(\widehat D-D^0)\|_2\le L_n\delta_{D,n}\), the asserted prediction bound follows.  This calculation explicitly retains both the Gram-perturbation and ridge terms multiplied by \(L_n\).

It remains to verify the affine conversion.  Collecting the coefficient of every cell in the displayed weight map gives
\[
 \sum_{j,\ell}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_at_a\sum_{j,\ell}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}\widehat S_{a,j\ell}
 =\widehat B-\widehat b^\top\widehat D.
\]
The same identity holds at the population coefficient.  By \(\mathrm{lem:normal-affine-identity}\), every coordinate of \(D^0\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_P\) and has mean zero.  Hence, for every \(b\), orthogonality gives
\[
 \|\phi_0-b^\top D^0\|_2^2
 =\|\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0\|_2^2
 +\|\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0-b^\top D^0\|_2^2.
\]
Thus the coefficient \(b_{J_n}\), defined by minimizing the left side on the positive Gram eigenspace, also minimizes the second term and attains \(\alpha_{J_n}\).  Under \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\),
\[
 \|B^0-b_{J_n}^\top D^0-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2
 =\|\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0-b_{J_n}^\top D^0\|_2
 \le\alpha_{J_n}.
\]
Adding the base-cell error, learned-dictionary prediction error, and sieve approximation gives \(O_p(\Gamma_n)=o_p(1)\), as claimed.

For \(i\in\mathcal I_k\), put
\[
 f_k=\widehat\psi^{(-k,C\mid A)}-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\), \(\max_k\|f_k\|_2=o_p(1)\).  Conditional on \(\mathcal D_{A,k}\vee\mathcal D_{C,k}\), the function \(f_k\) is fixed and the observations in \(\mathcal I_k\) are independent of it.  Therefore
\[
 E\!\left[\left.\left\{\sqrt n(P_{n,k}-P)f_k\right\}^2\right|\mathcal D_{A,k}\vee\mathcal D_{C,k}\right]
 \le C\|f_k\|_2^2=o_p(1),
\]
where fixed \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\) makes the fold-size factor bounded.  Conditional Chebyshev followed by a finite union bound gives
\[
 \sum_k\frac{|\mathcal I_k|}{\sqrt n}(P_{n,k}-P)f_k=o_p(1).
\]

For a learned cell, the two exact bridge identities at the base law give
\[
 P\{S_a(\widehat h,\widehat q)-S_a(h^0,q^0)\}
 =-E[I_a(\widehat q-q^0)(\widehat h-h^0)].
\]
Conditioning on \((A,Z,X)\) and on \((W,X)\), respectively, bounds its absolute value both by
\[
 \|T_a(\widehat h-h^0)\|_2\|\widehat q-q^0\|_2
 \quad\text{and by}\quad
 \|\widehat h-h^0\|_2\|T_a^*(\widehat q-q^0)\|_2.
\]
Summing over cells and using the total-variation envelope gives
\[
 \max_k|P\widehat\psi^{(-k,C\mid A)}-\theta(P)|
 \le CL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}
 =o_p(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Combining the conditional empirical term and this drift proves
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1).
\]
The summands on the right are i.i.d., mean zero, square-integrable, and have variance \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\).  They satisfy the Lindeberg condition because, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 E\!\left[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\mathbf 1\{|\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}|>\epsilon\sqrt n\}\right]\to0.
\]
The cited \(\mathrm{lem:lindeberg-feller-central-limit}\) therefore gives the asserted Gaussian limit.

For variance estimation, write \(\widehat\psi_i-\theta(P)=\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+f_{k(i)}(O_i)\).  Conditional Markov inequality gives
\[
 n^{-1}\sum_i f_{k(i)}(O_i)^2=o_p(1),
\]
because its conditional expectation is bounded by \(\max_k\|f_k\|_2^2=o_p(1)\).  Cauchy--Schwarz makes the empirical cross term with \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\) negligible.  To verify the remaining law of large numbers using only \(E\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2<\infty\), truncate \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\) at level \(M\).  Chebyshev's inequality handles the bounded truncated variables, while Markov's inequality bounds the empirical and population tails by \(E[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\mathbf 1\{\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2>M\}]\), which tends to zero as \(M\to\infty\).  Hence \(n^{-1}\sum_i\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)^2\to_pV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\).  Since \(\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)=O_p(n^{-1/2})\), centering by \(\widehat\theta_n\) does not alter the limit.  Thus \(\widehat V_n\to_pV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\), and positivity gives ratio consistency.  The product of the standardized numerator and \(\{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)/\widehat V_n\}^{1/2}\) consequently has the standard normal limit by the continuous-mapping argument; continuity of the normal distribution at \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\) proves pointwise Wald coverage.

Now impose the displayed locally uniform conditions.  Every preceding bound depends on the law only through \(\Gamma_n\), the mixed-bias gauge, the fold-size constant, and the stated moment envelopes.  Taking the supremum over \((s,t)\) in each conditional Markov or Chebyshev bound therefore yields
\[
 \sup_{s\in\mathcal S,|t|\le T}
 \left|\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P_{n,t,s})\}
 -n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})(O_i)\right|
 =o_{P_{n,t,s}}(1).
\]
The uniform \(L^2\) continuity and uniform integrability imply convergence of the corresponding variances, while the stated uniform Lindeberg condition and \(\mathrm{lem:lindeberg-feller-central-limit}\) yield the centered triangular-array Gaussian limit.  The assumed contiguity makes the base-law and local-law negligible remainders compatible, and the linear LAN term together with the displayed target expansion shows that centering at \(\theta(P_{n,t,s})\) removes exactly the local mean shift \(tE_P\{\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)s\}\).  Consequently the centered limit is \(N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}\), uniformly on the declared class.  The same uniform second-moment argument proves variance consistency.  This is precisely regularity on those contiguous path classes; because \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\) is the canonical gradient under \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), the limiting variance is the local efficiency bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:empirical-moment-perturbation}\), conditionally on every construction sigma-field \(\mathcal D_{A,k}\),
\[
 \|\widehat G_k^C-E[\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)}\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)\top}\mid\mathcal D_{A,k}]\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(\eta_{G,n}),
\]
and
\[
 \|\widehat c_k^C-E[\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)}\widehat B^{(-k,A)}\mid\mathcal D_{A,k}]\|_2=O_p(\eta_{c,n}),
\]
uniformly over the fixed number of folds.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a fold and condition on \(\mathcal D_{A,k}\); then the learned functions are fixed and the observations indexed by \(\mathcal C_k\) are independent.  The assumed moment-generating-function inequality and exponential Markov inequality give, for every unit \(u\) and every \(x>0\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\left|n_{C,k}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal C_k}X_{i,u}\right|>x\ \middle|\ \mathcal D_{A,k}\right)
 \le 2\exp\!\left[-c_1n_{C,k}\min\!\left\{\frac{x^2}{B_{D,n}^4},\frac{x}{B_{D,n}^2}\right\}\right].
\]
To see this, apply Markov's inequality to the exponential of the sum, multiply the conditional moment-generating-function bounds by independence, optimize \(\lambda\) over the permitted interval, and repeat with \(-\lambda\).  A maximal \(1/4\)-separated subset of the Euclidean unit sphere has at most \(9^{J_n}\) elements by comparing the volumes of disjoint radius-\(1/8\) balls with a radius-\(9/8\) ball.  For a symmetric matrix \(M\), approximation of a maximizing unit vector by this net gives \(\|M\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\max_u|u^\top Mu|\).  A union bound over the net, followed by the preceding tail inequality, proves the Gram rate; the displayed \(\log(1+J_n)\) factor is conservative relative to the net bound.

The same Chernoff calculation applied to \(Z_{i,u}\) gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\left|u^\top(\widehat c_k^C-E[\widehat D\widehat B\mid\mathcal D_{A,k}])\right|>x\ \middle|\ \mathcal D_{A,k}\right)
 \le2\exp\!\left[-c_2n_{C,k}\min\!\left\{\frac{x^2}{B_{D,n}^2B_{0,n}^2},\frac{x}{B_{D,n}B_{0,n}}\right\}\right].
\]
The same net and the identity \(\|v\|_2=\sup_{\|u\|=1}|u^\top v|\) yield the cross-moment rate.  Since \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\) is fixed, a final finite union bound makes both conclusions uniform in \(k\).

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(X_{n1},\ldots,X_{nk_n}\) be independent mean-zero real random variables.  If \(\sum_iE[X_{ni}^2]\to V\in(0,\infty)\) and, for every \(\epsilon>0\), \(\sum_iE[X_{ni}^2\mathbf 1\{|X_{ni}|>\epsilon\}]\to0\), then \(\sum_iX_{ni}\Rightarrow N(0,V)\).

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen iff is too strong: bridge existence and separate square integrability neither imply the little-o mixed-bias remainder nor force a Riesz representer to be an individual bridge-pair score. The replacement proves the strongest sound one-way result from an explicit pathwise product condition.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For the nested construction/calibration/evaluation estimator, under the construction-sample bridge rates, multiplier and calibration envelopes, Gram cutoff, affine coefficient envelope, and corrected projection balance, the exact cell expansion implies
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)}-D^0_{J_n}\|_{L^2(P;\ell^2)}=O_p(\delta_{D,n}),
 \qquad
 \delta_{D,n}=\left(\sum_{c=1}^{J_n}d_{c,n}^2\right)^{1/2}
 \le\sqrt{J_n}\max_{c\le J_n}d_{c,n}.
\]
The independent calibration sample satisfies the rates in \(\mathrm{lem:conditional-calibration-concentration}\).  If \(\Pi_{R,J_n}\) projects onto the positive population Gram eigenspace, then
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat\Pi_k^C-\Pi_{R,J_n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(\eta_{\Pi,n}),
\]
and
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat b^{(-k,C\mid A)\top}\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)}
 -b_{J_n}^\top D^0_{J_n}\|_2
 =O_p\!\left[L_n\delta_{D,n}
 +\frac{\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}}{\kappa_{J_n}}
 \left\{\zeta_{c,n}+(\zeta_{G,n}+\rho_n)L_n
 +\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}B_{0,n}\eta_{\Pi,n}\right\}\right].
\]
Consequently, whenever the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\) hold, the explicit coefficient-to-affine-weight identity gives
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat\psi^{(-k,C\mid A)}-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2
 =O_p(\Gamma_n)=o_p(1).
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old dimension-free rate and full-space ridge conclusion fail for a growing learned dictionary with a singular population Gram. The replacement uses dimension-correct aggregation, an independent calibration sample, a spectral cutoff, and the coefficient factors forced by the projected normal equation.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)<\infty\), fixed \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\), the nested-split conditions of \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\), and
\[
 \sqrt nL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}=o(1).
\]
Then, pointwise under \(P\),
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1)
 \ \Rightarrow\ N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\},
\]
\(\widehat V_n/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\to_p1\), and
\[
 P\{\theta(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha.
\]
For a locally uniform regularity extension, fix \(T<\infty\) and a class \(\mathcal S\) of bounded DQM path scores, and write \(P_{n,t,s}=P_{t/\sqrt n,s}\).  Suppose uniformly over \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(|t|\le T\): the construction-sample bridge and multiplier bounds defining \(d_{c,n}\) and \(d_{0,n}\), the sieve approximation \(\alpha_{J_n}\), the calibration exponential-moment and concentration bounds \(\eta_{G,n},\eta_{c,n}\), the positive-eigenvalue gap, cutoff stability, coefficient and weight envelopes, and \(\Gamma_n=o_p(1)\) all hold under \(P_{n,t,s}\); the root-\(n\) mixed-bias gauge is \(o_p(1)\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})\to\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\) in \(L^2\) and its squared family is uniformly integrable; and
\[
 \sup_{s,t}\left|\sqrt n\{\theta(P_{n,t,s})-\theta(P)\}-tE_P\{\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)s\}\right|\to0,
\]
\[
 \sup_{s,t}\left|\log\frac{dP_{n,t,s}^n}{dP^n}
 -\frac{t}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^ns(O_i)+\frac{t^2}{2}E_P[s^2]\right|=o_P(1),
\]
with a uniform Lindeberg condition for \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})\), and suppose the arrays \(P_{n,t,s}^n\) and \(P^n\) are mutually contiguous uniformly on the declared class.  Then the preceding asymptotic linear expansion, variance consistency, and centered Gaussian limit hold uniformly over \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(|t|\le T\).  In particular, the estimator is regular and locally efficient on every such uniformly controlled contiguous path class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original statement conflated pointwise inference with unquantified regularity along contiguous paths. The replacement proves pointwise inference from the corrected learned-signal lemma and states the locally uniform extension under explicit uniform sieve, nuisance, calibration, spectral, remainder, gradient, target, LAN, and Lindeberg conditions.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For each evaluation fold \(\mathcal I_k\), split its complement deterministically into disjoint index sets \(\mathcal A_k\) and \(\mathcal C_k\), with \(\min_k|\mathcal A_k|\wedge|\mathcal C_k|\ge c n\) for a fixed \(c>0\).  Fit every \(\widehat h_{aj}^{(-k,A)}\) and \(\widehat q_{a\ell}^{(-k,A)}\) using only \(\mathcal D_{A,k}=\sigma(O_i:i\in\mathcal A_k)\), and define \(\widehat S_{a,j\ell}^{(-k,A)}=S_a(\widehat h_{aj}^{(-k,A)},\widehat q_{a\ell}^{(-k,A)})\), \(\widehat B^{(-k,A)}=\sum_at_a\widehat S_{a,00}^{(-k,A)}\), and the pure-outcome, pure-treatment, and four-corner dictionary \(\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)}\) by the formulas in \(\mathrm{def:population-affine-sieve}\) with population cells replaced by these learned cells.  Conditional on \(\mathcal D_{A,k}\), evaluate these fixed functions only on \(\mathcal C_k\) and form
\[
 \widehat G_k^C=|\mathcal C_k|^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal C_k}
 \widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)}(O_i)\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)}(O_i)^\top,
 \qquad
 \widehat c_k^C=|\mathcal C_k|^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal C_k}

Assume the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)<\infty\), fixed \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\), the nested-split conditions of \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\), and
\[
 \sqrt nL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}=o(1).
\]
Then, pointwise under \(P\),
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1)
 \ \Rightarrow\ N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\},
\]
\(\widehat V_n/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\to_p1\), and
\[
 P\{\theta(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha.
\]
For a locally uniform regularity extension, fix \(T<\infty\) and a class \(\mathcal S\) of bounded DQM path scores, and write \(P_{n,t,s}=P_{t/\sqrt n,s}\).  Suppose uniformly over \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(|t|\le T\): the construction-sample bridge and multiplier bounds defining \(d_{c,n}\) and \(d_{0,n}\), the sieve approximation \(\alpha_{J_n}\), the calibration exponential-moment and concentration bounds \(\eta_{G,n},\eta_{c,n}\), the positive-eigenvalue gap, cutoff stability, coefficient and weight envelopes, and \(\Gamma_n=o_p(1)\) all hold under \(P_{n,t,s}\); the root-\(n\) mixed-bias gauge is \(o_p(1)\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})\to\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\) in \(L^2\) and its squared family is uniformly integrable; and
\[
 \sup_{s,t}\left|\sqrt n\{\theta(P_{n,t,s})-\theta(P)\}-tE_P\{\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)s\}\right|\to0,
\]
\[
 \sup_{s,t}\left|\log\frac{dP_{n,t,s}^n}{dP^n}
 -\frac{t}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^ns(O_i)+\frac{t^2}{2}E_P[s^2]\right|=o_P(1),
\]
with a uniform Lindeberg condition for \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})\), and suppose the arrays \(P_{n,t,s}^n\) and \(P^n\) are mutually contiguous uniformly on the declared class.  Then the preceding asymptotic linear expansion, variance consistency, and centered Gaussian limit hold uniformly over \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(|t|\le T\).  In particular, the estimator is regular and locally efficient on every such uniformly controlled contiguous path class.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct actual DQM paths whose scores densely span the annihilator of the outcome-solvability, treatment-solvability, and null-space-interaction normals on the full saturated fixed-defect joint-solvability germ, or exhibit a counterexample within that same germ.
open_obligations.obstruction: For the coupled nuisance \(\eta=(h_0,h_1,q_0,q_1)\), the frozen assumptions give only continuous transported operators and kernel projections. They do not establish the local product-parameter attainability or bounded-direction density required by the analogues of Chen--Santos Assumptions 4.1(iv)--(v), nor a locally onto chart for the common-law incidence map with its shared \((W,X)\) marginal.
open_obligations.attempted: I linearized the four residual components \(g_a-T_ah_a\) and \(1-T_a^*q_a\), quotiented nuisance directions by the two kernels, and checked the available perturbation result along DQM paths. It yields only \(o(1)\) motion of kernel projectors, not the first-order lifts needed to integrate an arbitrary element of \(\mathcal C_P^\perp\). The three positive finite germs verify the construction only in their certified finite incidence charts.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The finite-dimensional calculations establish reverse lifting on the regular \(36\)-cell rank-two germ, the singular two-branch \(3\)-by-\(3\) germ, and the transverse \(4\)-by-\(4\) rank-two germ with different arm row spaces.  For the unrestricted Hilbert germ, DQM and the frozen perturbation lemma yield only
\[
 \|\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P_t)-\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \vee
 \|\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P_t)-\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o(1).
\]
They provide neither an \(O(|t|)\) modulus nor a differentiable, locally onto chart for the coupled incidence map
\[
 (P',h_0,h_1,q_0,q_1)\longmapsto
 \bigl(g_a(P')-T_a(P')h_a,\ 1-T_a(P')^*q_a\bigr)_{a=0,1}
\]
after quotienting nuisance directions by \(\mathcal N_a(P)\) and \(\mathcal K_a(P)\).  Thus the analogues of Chen--Santos Assumptions 4.1(iv)--(v), especially attainability of bounded product directions and their density in \(\mathcal C_P^\perp\), are not consequences of the frozen primitives.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine whether pathwise differentiability on the unrestricted existence-only chart forces a square-integrable individual bridge-pair score, equivalently the missing necessity direction toward \(\Phi_P\neq\varnothing\).
open_obligations.obstruction: A Riesz representer on the actual tangent space need not factor through one outcome and treatment bridge pair, and separate \(L^2\) bridge assumptions do not control the products needed for that factorization.
open_obligations.attempted: I used bounded likelihood-ratio DQM differentiation and the exact primal-dual mixed-bias identity. These prove the sufficient direction under an explicit little-o product condition but do not yield the adjoint-range factorization required for necessity.
open_obligations.partial_result: The exact mixed-bias calculation proves that a square-integrable bridge-pair score is a gradient whenever nearby primal and dual representatives satisfy the displayed little-o product condition.  Tangent equality then makes the affine projection the canonical gradient.  What remains unproved is the converse: a continuous Riesz representer on \(\mathcal T_P\) need not, under the current existence-only and separate-square-integrability assumptions, factor as one square-integrable bridge-pair score.

prose_updates.tldr: The unrestricted score-lifting equality remains open: continuous moving kernels do not supply the coupled local parameterization required to realize every annihilator direction. The general efficiency result is therefore repaired to a proved one-way theorem: tangent equality plus one square-integrable bridge score and an explicit pathwise primal--dual product remainder yield the affine-quotient canonical gradient. The estimator is repaired by nested construction/calibration/evaluation splitting and calibration spectral cutoff. Under dimension-aware multiplier, concentration, cutoff, coefficient, approximation, and mixed-bias conditions it has pointwise asymptotic linearity, ratio-consistent variance, and Wald coverage; regularity is proved only for contiguous path classes satisfying the displayed uniform versions of every condition. The exact finite efficiency and nonattainment witnesses remain unchanged, and the observed bridge functional is a causal ATE only under the separate identification proposition.

project_justification.gap: Existing nonunique-bridge inference results do not identify the full tangent closure of the simultaneous outcome- and treatment-solvability germ. The remaining geometric gap is actual path realization on the unrestricted fixed-defect Hilbert stratum; pathwise differentiability alone also does not presently force an individual square-integrable bridge score.
project_justification.niche: The contribution isolates quotient-tangent efficiency with two nonunique bridge fibers and supplies a variance-minimizing affine estimator whose construction remains valid for singular population Grams through an independent calibration split and spectral cutoff.
project_justification.fill: The proved general results are the exact mixed-bias sufficient theorem, the affine Hilbert projection conditional on tangent equality, the dimension-aware nested calibration projection bound, pointwise efficient inference under explicit rates, and a locally uniform extension under fully quantified contiguous-path conditions. Reverse score lifting and the bridge-score necessity direction remain open; exact finite germs supply unconditional positive witnesses.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For each evaluation fold, its complement is split into construction and calibration samples of order \(n\). All bridge representatives and dictionary functions are learned only on the construction sample; the fixed learned dictionary is evaluated on the independent calibration sample to form a thresholded-and-ridged Gram projection; the resulting affine signal is evaluated only on the held-out fold. The conditions expose fourth-norm multipliers, square-root dimension aggregation, calibration exponential-moment rates, positive-eigenvalue and cutoff separation, coefficient and weight envelopes, sieve approximation, and the primal--dual mixed-bias product.

prose_updates.related_work: Bennett et al. provide the exact proximal mixed-bias architecture and product-rate logic, while Zhang et al. emphasize bridge nonuniqueness; neither is used to assert the unresolved tangent equality on this two-fiber saturated germ. Imbens et al., Ai--Shan, and uniqueness/surjectivity-restricted proximal efficiency results do not establish the quotient result here. Ai--Chen motivates Galerkin regularization, but the independent calibration layer, singular-Gram spectral cutoff, and affine coefficient accounting are explicit additional repairs. Chen--Santos identifies which local-product attainability and bounded-direction density facts would be needed for reverse lifting; those hypotheses have been audited and are not consequences of operator continuity. No claim relies on unverified publisher-only wording.
prose_updates.interpretation: With redundant proxies, a chosen bridge pair can have a valid pathwise score under the displayed product condition without minimizing variance over the affine score hull. When tangent equality is available, the nested affine projection supplies the variance-minimizing replacement and valid pointwise Wald inference under the corrected rates. For SUPPORT, bridge-dependent standard errors can therefore be compared with this affine replacement, but global efficiency on the unrestricted observed-law germ still requires score lifting, and causal interpretation still requires the separate latent identification conditions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The coupled score-lifting kernel is unresolved in the unrestricted Hilbert model. The frozen chart supplies continuous, not differentiable, moving kernel and cokernel projections and no locally onto parameterization of the joint solvability incidence set with a shared \((W,X)\) marginal. The proved estimator theorem is conditional on explicit construction, calibration, spectral, approximation, and mixed-bias rates; its regularity conclusion additionally requires their uniform versions, \(L^2\) continuity and uniform integrability of the canonical gradient, a uniform target expansion, LAN, and Lindeberg. Compact-operator closed-range collapse and rank-changing neighborhoods remain outside scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Unconditional claims remain the algebraic normal--affine identity, operator-kernel stability, and the certified finite tangent and nonattainment witnesses. In the general model, tangent equality is an unresolved premise. Conditional on that equality and the displayed nearby-bridge product condition, the affine projection is the canonical gradient. The repaired nested estimator attains pointwise Gaussian inference under explicit rates, and is regular and locally efficient only on contiguous path classes satisfying every displayed uniform condition. No iff between pathwise differentiability and bridge-score existence, no unqualified global efficiency, and no automatic causal interpretation are claimed.
